This integration of working together appeared before the Law in the person of Melchizedek, who is king of Salem and at the same time priest of the Most High God (Heb 7:1).
May the Lord give you wisdom in your hearts, that you may judge His people with righteousness, so that their good things may not vanish, and their glory remain throughout their generations [26].

If the seed of Aaron enjoyed the divine covenant for the practice of the priestly work, yet they needed prayer to be made for them; Sirach felt this, so he prayed for them, saying: "May the Lord give you wisdom in your hearts to judge His people with righteousness" [26].

This is what the deacon asks of the people in the Divine Liturgy and the liturgies, saying: "Pray and ask for our father the Pope the Patriarch," as he asks the same concerning the bishops, priests and deacons.

Why did Ben Sira pray for the high priests and the priests who were of the seed of Aaron? Without doubt Sirach's soul was bitter, because some persons bought the priesthood from the Seleucid kings in the second century BC to serve in the temple in Jerusalem. If the priest prays, asking blessing for the people, Ben Sira touches the blessing that descends upon the priests of God for the sake of their service to the people of God.
v Phinehas arose and made a triumph on account of the fornicators and showed his zeal: and how near he was to God.
His work bears witness to how vigilant his conscience was, for he drove fornication out of the camp by his righteousness.
Look at his deed, and from it learn his love: how much he cared to remove evil from his people.
His soul was holy and pure and hated fornication, so he threw the spear at the fornicators to put an end to evil.
He stood in prayer and held back death from many, and by the two persons whom he killed he saved thousands lest they be destroyed[7].
St. Jacob of Serugh Inspired by Sirach 45

entries.section: Reveal to me Your plan for me!

paragraphs.text: v How wonderful, how Pharaoh with all his might feared the Hebrew child Moses!
He was brought up in the house of the violent Pharaoh, and did not realize that the child who was in his house was a man of mercy!
Mercy did not leave his heart from his childhood to the day of his repose!
You granted him the spirit of strength and holiness, and he worked signs before kings.
You showed him Your glory and delivered to him the law.
You inclined Your ear, and found sweet his intercession for the people before You.
He was the object of Your delight for his faithfulness and meekness.
v You made a covenant with Aaron, and he put on the splendid garment of the priesthood.
With every step in the temple the heavenly ones rejoice at the sound of the bells on the hem of his garment!
He carries on his breastplate the names of the twelve tribes.
There was engraved on his turban "Holy to the LORD."
You accepted his daily sacrifices of the day and the night and his fragrant incense.
You raised him in the eyes of the heavenly and the earthly, since You did not give him a portion in the land of promise, for You are his portion.
v The heart of Phinehas, the grandson of Aaron, was kindled with the fear of God.
He would not accept silence over a priest who committed fornication with a pagan woman.
The soul of Phinehas was sanctified, and by his pure prayer death was held back from many!
What do I ask except that You lead my life in holiness and faithfulness.
So that I may have a portion in Your eternal embrace!

entries.section: 1. In praise of Joshua the son of Nun

paragraphs.text: 1 Joshua the son of Nun was valiant in the wars, the successor of Moses in the prophecies. 2 And he was, according to his name, great for the salvation of His elect, severe in vengeance on the enemies who withstood him, that he might give Israel an inheritance. 3 How great was his glory when he lifted up his hands and directed his spear against the cities! 4 Who stood before him like him in times past? For the Lord Himself delivered the enemies to him. 5 Did not the sun go back by his hand, and one day became as two? 6 He called upon the Most High, the Mighty One, when he was routing the enemies on every side, and the great Lord answered him with hailstones of mighty weight. 7 He made an assault on the nation in battle, and in the descent he destroyed those who withstood him, 8 that the nations might know all their armor, and that his war was before the Lord. Joshua was appointed as the successor of Moses in prophecy and in the leadership of the people (Deut 34:9-10), and Moses had earlier entrusted many works to him, regarding him as the faithful servant (Ex 17:9; 24:13), and before his departure he appointed him formally, before Eleazar the priest and the people, as his successor (Num 27:18-23; Deut 1:38), and after the death of Moses he prepared the children of Israel well for crossing the Jordan, and victory was achieved for him, and the inheritance of the nations (Josh 11:23).

Joshua the son of Nun was valiant in the wars, the successor of Moses in the prophecies, and according to his name he was great for the salvation of the elect, and for punishing the enemies who rose up against them, and for giving Israel its inheritance [1].

Ben Sira speaks of the commander-in-chief of the warriors, whom he called "valiant in the wars" [1]. The talk here is about the warriors, especially Joshua the son of Nun, Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and the judges, because Ben Sira was a contemporary of a priestly family that became a family of warriors, namely the Maccabees. These zealous priests drew the people to resist the occupier who insisted on defiling the Temple of the Lord, breaking the divine commandments, and accepting the worship of idols.

Ben Sira presented the work of God in the life of Joshua, who fought so that Israel might possess the Promised Land [1-6]. By this he supports his contemporaries in resisting the successors of Alexander the Great and working for the holiness of the house of the Lord and the Promised Land.

"Joshua was, according to his name, great for the salvation of the elect [1]," for its meaning is "the Lord saves." He led the people and defeated the Canaanites, beginning with the city of Jericho (Josh 6). He was a type of the awaited Messiah, our Savior, who was called Jesus.

entries.section: 1. In praise of Joshua the son of Nun

paragraphs.text: "The battles of the Lord": the heroism of Joshua was achieved by his hiding in the true Commander, the Lord Himself; therefore the battles of Joshua were called "the battles of the Lord" [3]. So also, to the extent that we hide in the Lord, believing in our spiritual striving that the two sides of the battle are the Lord Himself and the devil, our victory is achieved by our hiding in Him, and we are counted "soldiers of Christ" (2 Tim 2:3).

entries.section: 1. In praise of Joshua the son of Nun

paragraphs.text: The Lord moved nature to serve Joshua and his people (Josh 10:12-14), and He prolonged the day of the battle and made it as long as two days [4]. So also, when the Lord leads our battle against the devil, He grants us what seems impossible, since He directs everything for the sake of our victory. But the secret of Joshua's victory is that he did not fight with the sword only, but with prayer also, for he "called upon the Most High, the Mighty One" [5], "and the great Lord answered him."

He speaks here of Joshua's victory over Amalek (Ex 17:8-13). Moses needed Aaron and Hur to hold up his outstretched hands until the battle was ended, while Joshua continued to fight Amalek to the end.

v I pass on to Joshua the son of Nun, a type of the Lord both in name (Jesus) and in work, who crossed over into the Jordan, and subdued the hostile kingdoms, and divided the land among the victorious people; he who dealt with every city and village and mountain and river and hill and border, and imparted to him the kingdoms of the heavenly Jerusalem, that is, those that belong to the Church [1].
St. Jerome: How great was his glory when he lifted up his hands and stretched out his sword as a warning to the cities! [2]

His weapon was "lifting up his hands in prayer," and he had authority, so the sun did not go back, that is, it did not set until the victory was completed, for the day became as long as two days [4]. The lifting up of the hand here means declaring war on the enemies.
Who before him stood firm like him? For he is the one who led the wars of the Lord [3].
Joshua did not enter into a battle of his own; he did not defend himself, nor his dignity, nor seek any spoil, but hid in the Lord to lead "the battles of the Lord."
Did not the sun go back at a sign from his hand, and one day became as two? [4]

It is recorded in the history of Herodotus that the priests showed him documents indicating the existence of a day longer than usual; likewise in China they affirm that there was a long day in the reign of the Emperor "Yu," who was a contemporary of Joshua the son of Nun; and in Mexico there are documents indicating that a long day occurred in history in the same year in which Joshua was continuing his victories [2].
He called upon the Most High, the Mighty One, when the enemies were pressing him on every side.

entries.section: 1. In praise of Joshua the son of Nun

paragraphs.text: And the great Lord answered him with hailstones of mighty weight [5].

entries.section: 1. In praise of Joshua the son of Nun

paragraphs.text: He crushed those nations in the war, and on the slope of Beth-horon he destroyed those who withstood him, that the nations might know his complete armor, for he was fighting the war of the Lord [6].

Joshua went up to war against five kings, and the Lord Himself strengthened him, saying to him: "Fear them not: for I have delivered them into thine hand; there shall not a man of them stand before thee" (Josh 10:8). He came upon them suddenly, going up all night, and the Lord Himself discomfited the enemy and slew them with a great slaughter at Gibeon, and chased them along the way that goeth up to Beth-horon, and smote them to Azekah, and unto Makkedah... And as the enemy fled from before Israel, while they were on the descent of Beth-horon, the Lord cast down great hailstones from heaven upon them, and they were more which died with hailstones than they whom the children of Israel slew with the sword. It is as though the victory over these kings was achieved by two things: the sword and the hailstones coming down from heaven.
v Joshua the son of Nun, the righteous, who became a perfect disciple of the great Teacher (Moses), was also beautiful.
He also wished that the love of life might triumph in him, and that he might draw near to God in perfection.
He kept purity while serving in the tabernacle of time (the tent of meeting), and became for the people a second Moses before God.
He fought to establish the word of the Lord among the peoples, and the mighty works he wrought made known how exalted his beauty was [3].
St. Jacob of Serugh

entries.section: 2. In praise of Joshua and Caleb the son of Jephunneh

paragraphs.text: 8 For he followed the Mighty One. 9 And in the days of Moses he did a work of mercy, he and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, in that they stood against the enemy, and turned away the people from sin, and stilled the wicked murmuring. 10 And they alone were preserved of the six hundred thousand footmen, to bring them into the inheritance, into a land that floweth with milk and honey. 11 And the Lord gave strength unto Caleb, and it remained with him unto his old age; so that he went up to the high place of the land, which his seed obtained for an inheritance, 12 that all the children of Israel might see that it is good to follow the Lord.

And in truth he followed the Lord. Even in the days of Moses he showed his faithfulness, he and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, for they stood firm before the congregation, to keep the people from sin and to stop their wicked murmuring [7].

Sirach added to Joshua his famous companion Caleb the son of Jephunneh, recalling that the two urged Israel to victory over the holy land in the days of Moses [7-8]. In the days of Ben Sira there were many leaders who were turning away from divine wisdom and the commandment and were clinging to Hellenistic thought. Therefore Sirach presented these two men, whom the people resisted in the days of Moses, who persevered in spreading the spirit of faith and trust in the divine promises.

v When a man finds himself in a state that does not agree with his will and inclinations, he sees himself as in prison and torment. Therefore you must be content with what you have, so that you may not suffer (from your circumstances) and become ungrateful (and murmuring), and so wrong yourself without knowing it. But there is one way: despise temporal gifts [4].
St. Anthony the Great v Question: What if he obeys, but murmurs while he works?

Answer: The Apostle says: "Do all things without murmurings and disputings" (Phil 2:14). The murmurer turns aside from the unity of the brethren, and perhaps they will not use his work. For it is clear that such a one is afflicted with lack of faith and unsteadiness in hope [5].
St. Basil the Great And in truth they alone were preserved of the six hundred thousand footmen of the people, to enter into the inheritance, into a land flowing with milk and honey [8].

When Joshua and Caleb the son of Jephunneh gave their reports about the Promised Land, its good things, and its inhabitants, there was murmuring among the people and weeping, longing to return again to slavery under a new leader other than the prophet Moses. Therefore none of that generation entered the Promised Land except Joshua and Caleb.
And the Lord gave strength to Caleb, which remained with him until his old age, for he went up to the heights of the land which his seed kept as an inheritance [9].

Caleb gained great fame for his steadfastness in the commandment of the Lord while the majority opposed him. Caleb came to Joshua and said to him: "Behold, the Lord hath kept me alive, as he said, these forty and five years, even since the Lord spake this word unto Moses, while the children of Israel wandered in the wilderness: and now, lo, I am this day fourscore and five years old. As yet I am as strong this day as I was in the day that Moses sent me: as my strength was then, even so is my strength now, for war, both to go out, and to come in. Now therefore give me this mountain, whereof the Lord spake in that day; for thou heardest in that day how the Anakims were there, and that the cities were great and fenced: if so be the Lord will be with me, then I shall be able to drive them out, as the Lord said" (Josh 14:10-12).

entries.section: 2. In praise of Joshua and Caleb the son of Jephunneh

paragraphs.text: That all the children of Israel might see the goodness of following the Lord [10].
God raised Caleb and Joshua above the congregation in their generation, which revealed their following of the Lord (46:10).

13 And the judges, every one by his name, whose heart went not a whoring, nor departed from the Lord. 14 Let their memorial be blessed, and let their bones flourish out of their place. 15 And let their name be renewed, and let their sons glorify them.
And the judges also, each by his name, whose hearts did not fall into idolatry, and none of them departed from the Lord: may their memory be blessed! [11]

Sirach linked the judges with Joshua and Caleb without pointing to any of them by name. If Ben Sira began with Enoch up to Moses and Aaron as heroes of faith who entered into covenants with God and practiced worship to Him with sincerity, he now moves to heroes in military battles whose aim was to destroy the worship of idols, to worship God alone, and to establish a house for the Lord in which worship would be practiced through the generations. He then moves on to the prophet Samuel, at whose hands Saul and David the kings were anointed, one according to the desire of the people, and the other according to the mind of God [13].
And may their bones live again from their graves [6], and may the name of those honored live on in their sons! [12]

The words of the prophet Ezekiel about the resurrection of the dead (Ezek 37:1-14) were in his mind as he declared his faith in the resurrection from the dead. With burning zeal Ben Sira prays for his disciples and the whole new generation, that they may walk in the way of their fathers, the heroes of faith.

In his praise of the forefathers he gave a testimony to belief in the resurrection. "May their bones flourish" (46:12; 49:10). The flourishing of a plant signifies life. It is as though the dry bones enjoy the resurrection and life flourishes.

He also spoke of the prophet Elijah, whose return is expected to reform Israel (48:10). Solomon, who began his life with a spirit of godliness and wisdom, fell because of his bodily lusts. It is a lesson for believers, that no one should rely on being a member of the Church, nor on the holiness of his fathers, nor on the holiness he attained in his youth (Sir 49:4-5).
v Gideon was watchful, and Barak was full of faith, and Samson was a Nazirite, and Samuel was enlightened by prophecy [7].
St. Jacob of Serugh

entries.section: 4. In praise of the prophet Samuel

paragraphs.text: 16 Samuel, beloved of the Lord, a prophet of the Lord, established the kingdom, and anointed rulers over his people. 17 By the law of the Lord he judged the congregation, and the Lord looked upon Jacob. 18 By his faithfulness he was proved to be a prophet, and by his word he was known to be faithful in vision. 19 He called upon the Lord, the Mighty One, when his enemies pressed him on every side, and he offered a sucking lamb. 20 Then the Lord thundered from heaven, and with a great noise made his voice to be heard, 21 and destroyed the princes of the Tyrians, and all the lords of the Philistines. 22 And before the time of his long sleep, he made protestation before the Lord and his anointed, I have not taken any man's goods, so much as a shoe, and no man did accuse him. 23 And after his sleep he prophesied, and showed the king his end, and lifted up his voice from the earth in prophecy, to blot out the wickedness of the people.
The prophet of the Lord, Samuel, beloved of the Lord, established the kingdom and anointed rulers for his people [13].

Samuel is considered a symbol of the transition from the system of judges to the system of kings. Samuel, the last of the judges, also looked to not separating worship from the war against idols. Ben Sira took interest in the person of Samuel as the man of transition, who lived as a judge and a prophet in dark circumstances. The man of transition had to be marked by diverse aspects of leading the people and the leaders, so that he might succeed in fulfilling his mission. Samuel is one of the most beloved figures to the hearts of the Jews, for he combined in his person several qualities:
A. Prophet of the Lord, the first of God's prophets after Moses, who declared God's will and desire to the leaders as well as to the people [13].
B. Beloved of the Lord, a sign of a personal relationship with his Lord [13]. And he is faithful and trustworthy (1 Sam 9:6).
C. He kept the law of the Lord in his decisions and conduct [14].
D. He believed in the promises of the Lord to Jacob the son of Isaac the son of Abraham, "the Lord looked upon Jacob" [14].
E. He was marked by faithfulness and sincerity and the sanctification of his words, so he was known to be a true and honest prophet [15].

F. He was not like the other judges, the spiritual warriors, but was a prophet who established the school of the prophets, who taught the people the life of prayer and responding to the will of God. He was a spiritual leader who continued his work during the reign of King Saul and after the anointing of the prophet David as king.

G. He was a man of prayer [16] at the time when the people asked to have a king like all the nations, in whom they might glory. Although he opposed them, the Lord asked him to respond to their request after he warned them of what they would suffer from the king and his family and even his tribe.
He judged the congregation according to the law of the Lord, and the Lord looked upon Jacob [14].

What occupied the prophet Samuel was obedience to the divine commandment. When Saul exceeded his limits, disobeying the divine commandment by offering sacrifices that are the work of the priest and not the king, the prophet Samuel came to rebuke him, saying to him: "What hast thou done?" (1 Sam 13:11). Instead of examining himself and confessing his fault, he cast the blame on Samuel, saying: "Because I saw that the people were scattered from me, and that thou camest not within the days appointed, and that the Philistines gathered themselves together at Michmash; therefore said I, The Philistines will come down now upon me to Gilgal, and I have not made supplication unto the Lord: I forced myself therefore, and offered a burnt offering" (1 Sam 13:11-12).
By his faithfulness he proved that he was a true prophet, and by his words he was known to be a faithful seer [15].
All Israel from Dan even to Beer-sheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the Lord (1 Sam 3:20).
And so he called upon the Mighty Lord when his enemies troubled him on every side, and when he offered a little lamb [16].

entries.section: 4. In praise of the prophet Samuel

paragraphs.text: Then the Lord thundered from heaven, and with a great noise made His voice to be heard [17].

It refers to the victories of the Jews over the Philistines at Mizpeh (1 Sam 7:7-11), where the Lord thundered that day upon the Philistines and troubled them, so they were terrified and were smitten before them.

entries.section: 4. In praise of the prophet Samuel

paragraphs.text: And he destroyed the leaders of the people of Tyre, and all the lords of the Philistines [18].
And before the time of his everlasting sleep, he called the people to bear witness before the Lord and His anointed:

entries.section: 4. In praise of the prophet Samuel

paragraphs.text: "I have not taken any man's goods, so much as a shoe," and in truth no one accused him [19].

Ben Sira sees that death is a sleep of the body, while the soul departs to God. The prophet Samuel gave a plain farewell address in which he called them to witness before God and His anointed to his faithfulness toward them and that he had not exploited them, and he reminded them of the Lord's blessings and works with them, and rebuked them for asking for a king, opening before them the door of hope in the Lord who loves His people. What the prophet Samuel did here was not a defense of himself, for no one had accused him of anything, but he intended to instruct the new king. And as St. John Chrysostom says: [No one accused him; he did not utter this to justify himself, but because he had anointed a king, and he wanted to teach him to be meek and gentle under the cover of his defense of himself... He uttered this so that (the king) might be in a better condition [8].]

entries.section: 4. In praise of the prophet Samuel

paragraphs.text: And even after his sleep he prophesied and showed the king his end, and lifted up his voice from the earth in prophecy to blot out the wickedness of the people [20].

David's taking refuge with Achish put King Saul in a difficult position when the Philistines rose against Israel. But Saul, when danger came upon him and the Lord did not answer him because of his continual evils, took refuge with the woman who had a familiar spirit (1 Sam 28), although he had banned those with familiar spirits and wizards. He disguised himself, and asked her to bring up the spirit of Samuel that he might seek his counsel. The Book of Ben Sira says that God allowed him to speak with him in order to rebuke him for his evil conduct, and some think that Satan came in the form of Samuel to speak with him, because it is not possible for her to summon the spirits of the departed.
Inspired by Sirach 46

entries.section: Your hands train mighty giants of strength!

paragraphs.text: v The devil thought that Your people would collapse at the death of Moses.
Your hands which trained Moses, great among the prophets, trained his disciple Joshua!
Your voice resounds through the generations: "As I was with Moses, so I will be with thee" (Josh 1:5).
Moses could not cross the Jordan, yet behold, Joshua crossed it with the leaders and the people!
At a sign from his hand the sun stood still, and the day was prolonged to two days (Josh 10:12).
He took hold of the sword to fight, but You cast hailstones upon his enemies! (Josh 10:11)
v Joshua and Caleb entered the Promised Land, apart from all those who came out of Egypt.
Caleb grew old, but his strength never declined.
At the age of eighty-five his strength was as it was at forty.
You were glorified in the old man who went up to the heights of the land like a strong youth!
v Satan stirred up the pagan peoples so that they would not cease fighting the people of God.
And on the other hand, You sent pious judges who bear witness to You.
v The house of Eli the old priest became corrupt, and his two sons brought bitterness upon the people.
You visited Your people with a little child (Samuel). What shall we call him? You appeared to him and gave him the spirit of prophecy.
You called him Your beloved, for he clung to Your law.
He destroyed the leaders of the pagans, and his heart was not occupied with gold or silver.
He asked nothing of anyone, for You are his treasure.
His soul was embittered for the heart of the wicked King Saul.
You did not ignore his tears, and You anointed the greatest of kings, the prophet David!
Your hand, O my God, has wrought wonders, and still works, and will work until the day of Your final coming.
To You be glory, O mighty Shepherd of souls!

1 And after him rose up Nathan, and prophesied in the days of David. 2 As the fat is taken away from the sacrifice of salvation, so was David separated from among the children of Israel. 3 He played with lions as with kids, and with bears as if they had been lambs of the flock. 4 Did he not slay a giant when he was yet a youth? Did he not take away the reproach from his people, 5 when he lifted up his hand with the stone in the sling, and beat down the boasting of Goliath? 6 For he called upon the Lord the Most High; and He gave strength to his right hand, to slay a mighty warrior, and to exalt the horn of his people. 7 So the Lord gave him the glory of one who slays ten thousands, and praised him in His blessings, in that He brought to him the crown of glory. 8 For he destroyed the enemies on every side, and brought to naught the Philistines his adversaries, and brake their horn in sunder unto this day. 9 In all his works he gave thanks to the Holy One Most High with words of glory. 10 With his whole heart he sang praise, and loved Him that made him. 11 He set singers before the altar, and taught them sweet melodies. 12 He gave beauty to the feasts, and set in order the seasons unto the end, that they might praise His holy name, and that the sanctuary might sound from morning. 13 The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever; He gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Israel.

Sirach highlighted the following points: 1. David as a boy was a strong and courageous warrior in protecting the flock from lions and bears [3], and he also crushed Goliath the giant [4], and fought as a king against the Canaanites, especially the Philistines [5-7]. His main weapons in his battles were love for God and for his people and his prayers [5]; he did not forget to offer sacrifices of thanksgiving and praise to God, the Giver of victory [8-9]. 2. David's concern for communal worship [9] and for spreading the spirit of joy in the celebrations of the feasts [10]. 3. A man of sincere repentance, so he was made worthy to receive an everlasting royal covenant [11].
And after him rose up Nathan, to prophesy in the days of David [1].

He did not mention the fall of David, because his repentance wiped his sin from the record of his life. But lest we be lax about sin, he mentioned Nathan, who prophesied in his time, and who reproved the king for his sin and affirmed his need for firm discipline so that he might realize the bitterness of sin and not repeat it. The prophet Nathan rebuked King David for his fall into adultery with Bathsheba and for killing her husband in the battle (2 Kgs 12:1-15).
As the fat is taken away from the peace offering, so was David separated from among the children of Israel [2].
We should not be surprised at the comparison of David, the prophet and king, to the fat that is taken away from the peace offering. (See the appendix to this chapter.)
He played with lions as with young goats, and with bears as if they were lambs of the flock [3].

When Saul looked down on the youth David, and said to him: "Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth" (1 Sam 17:33). David answered him: "Thy servant kept his father's sheep, and there came a lion, and a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock: and I went out after him, and smote him, and delivered it out of his mouth: and when he arose against me, I caught him by his beard, and smote him, and slew him."
Did he not slay the giant in his youth, and take away the reproach from his people, when he lifted up his hand with the stone in the sling, and struck down the arrogance of Goliath? [4]

David went down with his staff and his sling and the smooth stones to strike the forehead of Goliath with a stone (1 Sam 17) and to kill him with his sword. His staff was a symbol of the Cross, and the stone is the Lord Christ (Ps 118:22), who kills the enemy.

St. Ambrose sees that the secret of David's victory is that he did not provoke the war, but Goliath was the one who began it, while David was driven into it by his spiritual zeal... He did not carry the weapons of Saul but his own sling and his staff... He entered the war after consulting the Lord. He says: [David did not provoke a war unless he was driven into it... His strength depended on his own arms and not on the weapons of others... He never entered a war without seeking the counsel of God [1].]

Would that in our spiritual striving we hold to these three things: that we do not push ourselves into the war by ourselves, but in humility flee from every stumbling block; then if we enter into a war, we carry our personal experience with our Lord and depend on His grace working in us, not on the prayers of others without striving on our part; and finally, that we do not go out to the war without seeking the counsel of the Lord and His help.
For he called upon the Lord the Most High, and strength was given to his right hand to overcome the mighty man in battle, and to exalt the horn of his people [5].
David took the instruments of Goliath to his tent, so that the energies that had been working for the kingdom of the devil might work for the Kingdom of God.
So they gave him the glory of one who slays ten thousands, and praised him with the blessings of the Lord, offering him the crown of glory [6].

The women received Saul and David, some of them singing to them and others beating the timbrels and triangles and repeating the refrain: "Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands" (1 Kgs 18:2). Instead of rejoicing in David's success, Saul began to hate David, watching him. Envy filled the heart of Saul, and he wanted to be rid of David, who had saved him from his enemies. He wanted to kill David, and so became a bad example of anger and envy.
For he destroyed the enemies on every side, and brought to naught the Philistines who withstood him, and brake their power in sunder unto this day [7].
In every work of his he gave thanks to the Holy One Most High with a word of praise. And with his whole heart he sang a song of praise, and loved Him that made him [8].
David, the man of God, offered sacrifices of thanksgiving and praise as was his custom with all his heart, so his heart was counted like the heart of God (1 Kgs 13:13).
He set the singers of psalms before the altar, to send forth sweet melodies with their voices [9].

David made great preparations before his death. He did not prepare anything for the day of his death, but for the building of the house of the Lord. He devoted his life to a series of battles, not for the extension of the kingdom, but to gather materials for building the house of the Lord. In appearance he was one of the greatest heroes of war, while inwardly his heart was occupied with the building. St. Jacob of Serugh presents to us a wonderful picture of the feelings of King David as he was preparing to depart from the world, saying:
[When the one skilled in knowledge knew that his appointed time had come, he wished to show his love for the Lord plainly.
He saw death coming to dissolve the temple of his body, so he wished to build a holy temple for the Lord his God.
The prophet saw that the fabric of his body was almost worn out, so he wished to build the Holy of Holies for Him who holds the ends of the earth.
And when he showed the idea of building a temple, his Lord spoke to him by the Spirit, saying:
"O son of Jesse, build not for Me a temple of stones, for the heart of the righteous alone can contain Me, that I may be honored in it (2 Sam 7:5; Isa 66:1; Acts 7:46-50).
Heaven and earth with their bounds cannot contain Me, for only the heart of the righteous, and no other, can hold Me.
I am honored and sanctified in the pure soul, and a building made by the hands of men cannot contain Me.
Heaven, which is My throne, cannot hold Me in its bosom, and the earth alone is My footstool (Ps 99:5).
I have measured the heaven of the Most High with a span as One who knows all, and I have measured the dust of the earth in My hand as the Almighty (Isa 40:12).
Build not for Me a temple for My glory where I am to be honored, for your fingers have shed much of the blood of men.
Your son shall build Me a house to dwell in and to be sanctified in, and if it be well pleasing to Me, I shall be with him as I was also with you [2].]

He gave the feasts their honor, and arranged their times throughout the year, that they might praise the holy name of God, and that the sanctuary (the Temple) might resound from the early morning [10].

King David contributed the huge preparation for building the Temple in the days of his son Solomon, and encouraged the leaders and the people to contribute to the cost of the building. His wonderful efforts in organizing the choirs of praise and arranging the service of the feasts and of worship reveal what was in the heart of David. It did not concern him that the Temple be erected in his reign or that of his son, nor to estimate the cost of the building of the Temple, but he wanted to see the Temple as an icon of heaven rejoicing in the Lord, looking for every member of the people to contribute to the building of the Temple by enjoying the pledge of heaven.

Wherever David was, even in his flight from the face of Saul, who was determined to kill him, his harp and his praises did not leave him, so that heaven was not far from him, enjoying the divine presence under all circumstances.
The Lord forgave his sins, and exalted his standing [3] for ever, and gave him a covenant of kings and a throne of glory in Israel [11].

The covenant that the Lord made with David (2 Kgs 7:16) is that He would establish his throne for ever. This was fulfilled by the Incarnation of the Word of God from St. Mary, of the seed of David, and He is the King of kings. He establishes His Kingdom in the hearts of His believers from all the nations and peoples.

14 After him rose up a wise son, and for his sake he dwelt at large. 15 Solomon reigned in days of peace, and God brought him rest on every side, that he might build a house for His name, and prepare a sanctuary for ever. 16 How wise wast thou in thy youth, and filled with understanding as a flood! For thy mind covered the earth, 17 and thou filledst it with dark parables. Thy name went far unto the islands; and for thy peace thou wast beloved. 18 The countries marvelled at thee for thy songs, and proverbs, and parables, and interpretations, 19 in the name of the Lord God, who is called the God of Israel. 20 Thou didst gather gold as tin, and didst multiply silver as lead.

David fell asleep while preparing the whole kingdom to fulfill the desire of his heart to build a house for the Lord, and he had devoted his resources for this work, and here he hands over the throne to Solomon, for no purpose except to fulfill the divine promise to him that his son would build the Temple. He fell asleep with a rejoicing heart, for he is a man of praise, feeling as one sharing the rejoicing life of the heavenly beings, and here his son Solomon builds the Temple, the house of praise and worship.

The Second Book of Chronicles begins with Solomon, whose main work was building the Temple as a center for the whole earth, declaring the divine presence. The book concentrated on the house of David so that believers might seek the Son of David dwelling in their midst and in their hearts. David fell asleep while preparing the whole kingdom to fulfill the desire of his heart to build a house for the Lord, and he had devoted his resources for this work, and here he hands over the throne to Solomon, for no purpose except to fulfill the divine promise to him that his son would build the Temple. He fell asleep with a rejoicing heart, for he is a man of praise, feeling as one sharing the rejoicing life of the heavenly beings, and here his son Solomon builds the Temple, the house of praise and worship.
After him rose up his wise son, who lived in a spacious place for his sake [12].

The period from the accession of Solomon to the throne in 961 BC until the captivity of Jerusalem by the Babylonians in 587 BC is long; he did not mention all the heroes of faith in that period, besides the fact that many of the kings in this period despised divine wisdom.
Solomon reigned in days of peace, and God gave him rest on every side, that he might build a house for His name, and prepare an everlasting temple [13].

Ben Sira was concerned to highlight what Solomon did to embrace heavenly wisdom, namely the building of the house of the Lord, where worship is practiced for the sanctification of the people [13], and his concern for songs, proverbs, wise sayings and interpretations [17].

Solomon built the Temple of the Lord in Jerusalem, and it was rebuilt by King Herod, and this building was contemporary with the coming of the Lord Christ, who prophesied its complete destruction (Mt 23:38-39), and that He would raise up a new temple, which is His body risen from the dead.
How wise you were in your youth! And full of understanding like a river! [14]

The Lord appeared to Solomon and asked him what he desired, and Solomon chose wisdom and did not ask for glory or riches (1 Kgs 3). God gave him what he asked and what he did not ask. He prayed, saying: "And thy servant is in the midst of thy people which thou hast chosen, a great people, that cannot be numbered nor counted for multitude. Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad: for who is able to judge this thy so great a people?" (1 Kgs 3:8-9). It is said in the Book of Wisdom: "Wisdom is better than strength: and a wise man than a mighty man" (Wis 6:1). "Wisdom is glorious, and never fadeth away: yea, she is easily seen of them that love her, and found of such as seek her" (Wis 6:13).
Your soul covered the earth, and you were filled with parables and riddles [15].

"And God gave Solomon wisdom and understanding exceeding much, and largeness of heart, even as the sand that is on the sea shore" (1 Kgs 4:29). The secret of Solomon's glory is in the wisdom which he received as a gift from God, more than in wealth. Solomon experienced it as a divine gift, for he says: "For the Lord giveth wisdom: out of his mouth cometh knowledge and understanding" (Prov 2:6). And it is said in the Book of Job: "Who hath put wisdom in the inward parts? or who hath given understanding to the heart?" (Job 38:36).
Your name reached the far islands, and you became beloved for your peace [16].
And at your songs and your proverbs and your wise sayings the nations marvelled at you because of your interpretations [17].

Solomon was concerned to spread the spirit of wisdom among the nations; Solomon is counted unique in his concern for preaching to the nations through songs, proverbs, wise sayings and interpretations, and in being an example even to pagan kings in his work as a king.
The queen of Sheba marvelled at the wisdom of Solomon (1 Kgs 10): the queen confessed that what she saw was greater than what she had heard about him.
The greatness of his wealth: the queen of Sheba offered him much gold, spices and precious stones, and the kings of the surrounding nations also offered him in abundance.
The greatness of his generosity: much came to him, and he also gave much.
The greatness of his appearance: shields of gold, cups of gold, a throne unique in greatness.
The greatness of his power: chariots and horses in abundance [26].
His commercial ability: trade exchange with Egypt [28-29].
The wealth of his people: [27].

If all things are put together, it may be said that he surpassed all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom at that time; he was a shadow of Christ, who said: "Behold, a greater than Solomon is here" (Mt 12:42; Lk 11:31).
In the name of the Lord God, who is called the God of Israel, you gathered gold as tin, and multiplied silver as lead. [18].

21 Thou didst bow thy loins unto women, and by thy body thou wast brought into subjection. 22 Thou didst stain thy honor, and pollute thy seed: so that thou broughtest wrath upon thy children, and wast grieved for thy folly. 23 So the kingdom was divided, and out of Ephraim ruled a rebellious kingdom. 24 But the Lord will never leave off His mercy, neither shall any of His works perish, neither will He abolish the posterity of His elect, and the seed of him that loveth Him He will not take away. 25 Wherefore He gave a remnant unto Jacob, and out of him a root unto David.

After Solomon received great wisdom, fame and wealth from God, he went down and brought shame upon himself [20], and even enslaved himself to sexual passions. But God in His great mercy did not forsake him [22] for the sake of his father David, and indeed the Christ was born of the seed of David [22].
But you lay down beside women, and your body enslaved you [19].

His success is counted a testimony to God among the nations; yet with all the wisdom that marked him he fell into slavery to bodily lusts [19]. He turned away from true and pure worship through the seduction of his wives, a matter to which Holy Scripture pointed after several centuries (Neh 13:26); therefore God allowed him to be disciplined [9:11-40]. Solomon, who had consecrated his heart to the love of God, turned it to foreign women. Solomon, who began by shepherding his people with love, was occupied with his private palace and huge constructions, and so burdened his people with taxes and forced labor.

If Ben Sira himself followed in the footsteps of the wisdom of Solomon, then by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit he recorded this book in the pattern of the Book of Proverbs, though he affirms that the wise Solomon became corrupt because of his enslavement to idolatries and his withdrawal from the faith of his fathers.

v If you read again what was written about Solomon, you find that, although he was exceedingly wise (Eccl 12:9), he "drew near to many women," while the law of God says: "Neither shall he multiply wives to himself, that his heart turn not away" (see Deut 17:17). Despite the greatness of his wisdom and the greatness of his standing before God, he was deceived, because he gave himself over to many women. I think that the many women point to the many doctrines and the different philosophies that men have, which he, being a man rich in knowledge and wisdom, wanted to know and examine. He was not able to keep himself within the judgment of the divine Law.
He was seduced by the philosophy of Moab, which urged him to offer sacrifices to the idol of Moab. The same applies to the Ammonites and the other peoples.

It is said that he welcomed many women and built temples and offered sacrifices to their idols. Truly, it is a great thing to mingle with many doctrines as with women and yet not turn aside from the judgment of the truth, but to say firmly: "There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, and virgins without number. My dove, my undefiled is but one; she is the only one of her mother, she is the choice one of her that bare her" (Song 6:8-9) [4].
Origen: You brought a stain upon your glory, and defiled your seed, and brought wrath upon your sons, and they were pierced by your folly [20].
Therefore the kingdom was divided into two, and a rebellious kingdom arose out of Ephraim [21].

v Wisdom can be the greatest help in keeping company with the strongest men of the city, and it also usually knows when to exclude those who fail in doing their duty. For there has never been anyone who did not stumble. As for the words of the wicked, we must not give them final consideration, lest, hearing with your ears what is against you, you are then stung in the heart, and the reaction is your attacking him.

Although I knew all these things and had received wisdom from God, when I cast it from me I was no longer what I had been. For wisdom forsook me for a while to a distance that is hard to measure, so that it seemed it would never be mine. At last I stopped seeking it altogether, and I no longer cared to reckon my folly and my empty lusts and life of amusement [5].

St. Gregory the Wonderworker: But the Lord did not forsake His mercy, nor corrupt any of His words, nor blot out the seed of His elect (David), nor destroy the seed of him who loved Him, but He left a remnant for Jacob, and a root of his lineage for David [22].

For the sake of King David, the righteous, the Lord proclaimed His mercy, which was manifested in the following: 1. The repentance of Solomon and his return from corruption and his clinging to the Lord. 2. There were found among the kings of Judah (the southern kingdom) some godly ones who walked like their father David. 3. He left a holy remnant for Jacob, and the Lord allowed the discipline of Israel by the Assyrian captivity and the discipline of Judah by the Babylonian captivity, but He raised up Cyrus king of Persia to allow the Jews to return to the Promised Land. 4. The Lord raised up heroes of faith even in the land of captivity, such as Esther and Haman and the prophets Daniel and Ezekiel and others, and leaders such as Zerubbabel and Nehemiah and Ezra the scribe, etc. 5. The Lord did not break His covenant with David, so the Wisdom of God came incarnate from St. Mary, the daughter of David, and the incarnate King of kings established His Kingdom in the hearts of believers, and made of them a holy temple for Himself in which the Holy Spirit dwells.

entries.section: 4. The rebellion of Jeroboam and the division of the kingdom

paragraphs.text: 26 And Solomon rested with his fathers, 27 and left behind him of his seed one foolish among the people, 28 even Rehoboam, of little understanding, who turned away the people through his counsel, 29 and Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, and gave Ephraim a way of sin. And their sins were multiplied exceedingly, 30 until they were removed out of their land, 31 and sought out all wickedness, till the vengeance came upon them.

The degradation of Solomon through his slavery to lusts bore fruit in the division of the kingdom immediately after his death. Corruption passed to his sons, beginning with Rehoboam [23]. Because of his indulgence in lusts and his rebellion against the divine commandment, Solomon took foreign wives who worshiped idols. So he planted the seeds of rebellion and disobedience in his son Rehoboam. This is what he also planted in his former servant Jeroboam, who turned from a friend of Solomon and his seed into a rebellious enemy. The rebellion of both Rehoboam and Jeroboam led to the division of the kingdom into a northern kingdom comprising ten tribes under the leadership of Jeroboam, and a southern kingdom comprising two tribes, Judah and Benjamin. This division drove the ten tribes to become estranged from Jerusalem and the Temple and the Levitical priesthood, and to be plunged into idolatry.
When Solomon rested with his fathers, he left after him one of his sons, lacking prudence and understanding.
Rehoboam, who by his counsel led the people to rebel [6] [23].
Two kings succeeded Solomon, one in the south, his son Rehoboam, and the second in the north, his enemy Jeroboam, and both of them were foolish [23].
Likewise there was Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who drove Israel to sin, and led Ephraim in the way of sin, and their sins were multiplied exceedingly until He removed them from their land [24].
They sought after all evil, until the punishment came upon them [25].
v Question: How can we fear the judgment of God (Heb 27:10)?

Answer: The expectation of anything terrifying drives a person to fear. So we fear wild beasts, and also rulers, expecting some evil from them. Therefore if a person believes that God's warnings about the final judgment are true, and expects that it is fearful and terrifying, it is natural for him to fear the judgments of God [7].
St. Basil the Great Inspired by Sirach 47

entries.section: Fence me about with Your grace, lest I collapse

paragraphs.text: v Whenever I look at Rehoboam the son of Solomon the son of David, my depths cry out to You that my soul may not perish.
Rehoboam did not learn from his father Solomon, so as to ask wisdom of You.
He took the counsel of the wicked, and was arrogant toward the people.
So all that his wise father and his godly grandfather had gathered was lost.

v The young Solomon began to rule, and he asked for wisdom that he might hand over the leadership of the kingdom into Your hand; he increased in glory and wisdom and wealth, and the world was amazed at his wisdom.
But he became careless, and gave over his loins beside pagan women.
He brought a stain of shame upon his glory, and defilement upon his seed, and wrath upon his sons.
Yes, he repented, but his son Rehoboam had absorbed corruption from him in the period of his deviation!
v And what shall I say of David, the grandfather of Rehoboam? In his early youth he tore a lion and a bear with his hands.
He faced Goliath the giant, not with sword and spear, but in Your name, O Lord of hosts, and he crushed his arrogance against You.
His life was an unbroken series of praises and thanksgivings to You.
He established holy choirs that praise with the heavenly beings.
He organized the joyful feasts, and prepared many for the everlasting heavenly feast.
One day he grew lax, and descended from sin to sin. So You sent him the prophet Nathan to bring him back to You by repentance.
There is no one, even a great prophet or a king beloved by You and by men, who is immune from error!
Fence me about, O Lord, lest I grow lax like great David, nor give myself up to careless gatherings like wise Solomon, nor run after unfitting friendships like Rehoboam!
There is none to protect me from my weaknesses except Your Holy Spirit!
Appendix to Sirach 47: David the prophet and the fat in the peace offering. Ben Sira compares the prophet David among the children of Israel to the fat in the peace offering (Sir 47:2; Lev 3).

First: As for the peace offering, Origen [8] sees it as the offering of the perfect man, or the spiritually mature, who enjoys the perfect peace of God in his inner life, and as an overflow of peace and thanksgiving springing from the Lord Christ, the Giver of peace. Therefore it is called "the offering of perfection."

Second: As for the fat, in the Old Testament the eating of blood and fat was forbidden, because the blood points to the life of man, and the fat is the best part of the animal. The commandment came in the peace offering that the man who eats the fat of this sacrifice shall be cut off from the people of God (Lev 3:16). The fat was offered to the Lord and man had no share in it, a sign of offering the best thing in the sacrifice to the Lord. And when Eli the priest was lax with his two sons the priests, letting them eat the fat of the sacrifices, the Lord rebuked him, for he honored his sons above the Lord (1 Sam 2:29).

It is said of the peace offering: "And he shall offer of the sacrifice of the peace offering an offering made by fire unto the Lord; the fat thereof, and the whole rump, it shall he take off hard by the backbone; and the fat that covereth the inwards, and all the fat that is upon the inwards, and the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, and the priest shall burn them upon the altar: it is the food of the offering made by fire unto the Lord" (Lev 3:9-11).

Third: David and his being chosen from among Israel is likened to the fat in the best sacrifice, which belongs to the perfect. He is the portion of the Lord, for he consecrated all his life, and especially his heart and his thought and his emotions, to the Lord alone. So David was a living model of those who do what is right in the eyes of the Lord (1 Kgs 11:33; 2 Kgs 22:2; 2 Chr 28:1).
This is the personality which enjoyed the divine promise that from its seed one would sit on the throne for ever.

Ben Sira presents David as the best of the perfect ones, and yet with this loftiness he was not immune from error; and when he was lax in the purity of his heart he fell into sins into which he had not fallen in his boyhood and youth. Truly, he spent the rest of his life practicing repentance with a spirit of hope and certainty in the love of God who forgives sins!

[What is wonderful in the plan of God is that the drinking of blood and the eating of fat are harmful to man's health; and at the same time the Law forbade eating them because they are the portion of the Lord.]

entries.section: 1. In praise of the prophet Elijah

paragraphs.text: 1 And Elijah the prophet stood up as fire, and his word burned like a torch. 2 He brought a famine upon them, and by his zeal he made them few in number. 3 By the word of the Lord he shut up the heaven, and brought down fire from it three times. 4 How glorious wast thou, O Elijah, in thy wondrous deeds! And who hath glory like unto thee? 5 Thou who didst raise up a dead man from death, and from hell, by the word of the Most High. 6 Who broughtest kings down to destruction, and the proud ones from their beds. 7 Thou who heardest the judgment in Sinai, and in Horeb the sentences of vengeance. 8 Who anointedst kings for vengeance, and prophets to succeed after thee. 9 Who wast taken up in a whirlwind of fire, in a chariot of fiery horses. 10 Who wast ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath before it break forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father unto the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob. 11 Blessed are they that saw thee, and they that have obtained the glory of thy friendship. 12 For we shall live this life, but after death we shall not have such a name.
Then stood up Elijah the prophet as fire, and his word was kindled like a lamp [1].

Ben Sira highlighted what marked the prophet Elijah, the man of faith: a fiery heart kindled with zeal for the word of God and for worship of Him, not of idols; therefore it was said of him: Elijah the prophet stood up as fire to burn up evil, stubbornness and resistance to God, especially on the part of King Ahab and his wife Jezebel. And at the same time his word was kindled like a lamp that enlightens the souls longing for the truth in the midst of the pitch darkness of corruption. Elijah was a great prophet, although in human weakness he feared the wicked queen Jezebel, who dominated the personality of her husband King Ahab and corrupted his faith, and killed many of the prophets (1 Kgs 18-19), and at the same time Ahab and Jezebel were in great terror of him.

It is said of the angels that they are God's servants, burning with the fire of holy zeal (Ps 104:4); Elijah imitated them, so he brought down fire three times (2 Kgs 1:10-14), and was taken up to heaven in a chariot of fiery horses (2 Kgs 2:11). Elijah did not die, and his coming is awaited together with Enoch, to resist the antichrist and support the believers at that time.

entries.section: 1. In praise of the prophet Elijah

paragraphs.text: It is he who brought a famine upon them, and by his zeal made them few in number [2].

entries.section: 1. In praise of the prophet Elijah

paragraphs.text: By the word of the Lord he shut up the heaven, and brought down fire three times [3].

If sin has corrupted our life and made of us a land that brings forth thorns and thistles (Gen 3:18), then we have become in need of the word of God, the consuming fire, to burn up these thorns and thistles.

v In truth there are thorns that are not scattered, but are in the hands of the one who is drunk with vice and are driven deep into it, so that the person forgets his sobriety, and as it is said in the Proverbs, "thorns hidden in the hands of the drunkard" (see Prov 26:9).

Must we not speak words describing any disturbances that sow evils which afflict the one who receives them in the very being of his soul? He who receives deep moral evil in his soul, so that it becomes a land that brings forth thorns (Gen 3:18), needs the word of the living God to cut it off from its roots, which is more terrible and sharper than a two-edged sword, and hotter than fire [1].

v He who adds evil in the depths of his soul until it becomes a land that brings forth thorns needs to have this cut off by the living and active word of God, which is sharper than any two-edged sword and more able than any fire to burn (Heb 4:12; Sir 48:1). That fire which exposes the thorns, and which by its divinity stops them! So the threshing floors and the fields of wheat have no need of (another) fire to be sent to such a soul [2].
Origen: By your wonders you were honored, O Elijah! And who can glory like you [3]? [4]
v Who will make room for my word to tell his beauty (the beauty of Elijah) from his childhood, in what life he was brought up?
Who will give me a book to help me look and see how radiant with holiness he was from his youth?
His lofty and spiritual beauty is hidden from me; how did he begin to walk on his way toward God?
Scripture showed his story to the world only here, when he withheld the rain and the dew because of Ahab (1 Kgs 17:1).
Up to here the way of his righteousness and the beauty of his conduct and the excellence of his virginity were hidden.
From here Scripture began to relate his story, because on account of the iniquity of Ahab he bound the heaven with one word.
You, then, consider from before this great work, how many were his works and labors for the sake of God?
And therefore Scripture hid his life, because it was lofty, and we could not speak of it.
From his childhood he held fast to a great way of life, with victorious works, such that even nature could not bear them.
As soon as he knew the difference between good and evil, he began with the good, and evil never overcame him.
As soon as he knew the world, he left it lest he live in it, and loved the wilderness and dwelling alone on the mountains.
And as soon as he felt that there was another world of God, he set his face toward it, running to reach it.
As soon as he saw that this world is passing away, he did not stoop to its company, nor to work in it.
As soon as he heard that this place was not his place, he no longer loved it, and did not wish to come near its deeds.
From the time he knew that there is another life of God, he sought for it with great labors in order to inherit it.
As soon as he understood that Adam died when he transgressed the commandment, he did not turn aside from the spiritual law.
He looked at (human) nature (and understood) that if it had not sinned it would not have died, so he was terrified of sin, lest he become a fruit of death.
Since he knew what death is and what life is, he wrestled for life so as to acquire it.
From his youth he was brought up spiritually toward the great height until he reached this rank, the highest of all.

entries.section: 1. In praise of the prophet Elijah

paragraphs.text: He looked to God, and as soon as he knew how beautiful He is, he no longer turned his gaze away from Him to see anything (else) [4].

entries.section: 1. In praise of the prophet Elijah

paragraphs.text: St. Jacob of Serugh: You raised a dead man from death, and from Hades by the word of the Most High [5].

The prophet Elijah raised the son of the widow of Zarephath, the Gentile woman (1 Kgs 17:1-24). Elijah stretched himself upon the dead child three times, crying to the Most High to restore the child's life; this points to his taking refuge in the Holy Trinity, the Giver of life.
v The widow's son died, because the son of the Church, that is, the Gentiles, died because of their many sins and transgressions.
Through the prayers of Elijah the widow's son recovered life; and by the coming of Christ the son of the Church, that is, the Christian people, came out of the prison of death.

Elijah bowed down in prayer, and the widow's son recovered life. So Christ plunged into His sufferings, and the Christian people recovered life. Why did Elijah bow down three times to raise the boy?.. In truth he bowed down three times, showing the mystery of the Trinity. The whole Trinity restored life to the widow's son, or to the Gentiles. Moreover, this is fulfilled in the sacrament of Baptism, where the old man is immersed in the water three times so that the new man may be made worthy to rise [5].

entries.section: 1. In praise of the prophet Elijah

paragraphs.text: St. Augustine: And you brought down kings to destruction, and those who were glorified from their beds [6].
v The Lord called His righteous servant and spoke with him: Arise, go down to meet Ahab the king (1 Kgs 21:17-18), and expose his lie.
Behold, he has gone down to inherit the seized vineyard. Go and tell him: You shall not enjoy an inheritance that is not your own.
Go and tell this one who killed and thought he had inherited: Naboth has handed his vineyard over to Me, and he is dying.
I, I am the heir of that meek one, and the vineyard is My possession, and I stand over his inheritance, and I execute his judgment.
What do you want from the possession handed over into My hands? He called upon Me as he was being stoned and commanded me, and I will not neglect it.
I demand justice to avenge Naboth and every wronged one, for his judgment is kept for Me, and I will not keep silent.
In the place where the dogs licked his blood they shall lick your blood (1 Kgs 21:19); behold, you are repaid with the measure of blood with which you also measured (Mt 7:2)...
He goes forward boldly to drive the king from the inheritance, armed with the Lord, and he takes no account of the kings of the earth.
And righteousness and uprightness follow him, and faith and perfection run with him (Ps 85:10-11).
He despised the crown, because the smell of iniquity rose from it, and he made light of authority greatly without fear.
And as Ahab was standing in the vineyard which he had gone down to inherit, he saw Elijah coming, and the wicked one trembled.
The prophet met the king like the thief and the master of the house, and the plunder was not hidden.
He caught him in a vineyard whose owner had been killed on his account, and the king was ashamed before the sight of the blood he had shed.
The king said: "Hast thou found me, O mine enemy?" (1 Kgs 21:20). He was indeed the enemy of the house of God and of the prophet.
The partner of the idols and of the gods of the Amorites showed himself how he hated the servants of the Lord.
There was great enmity between him and the Lord, because he was a friend of all the gods of the Canaanites.
And as the prophet stood before him rebuking him, he was his enemy, as he called him and exposed himself.
The righteous one said: Yes, I have found you as you said, for you cannot hide your iniquity from the Lord.
Your hands are full of innocent blood, so how will you be justified? Seizure and plunder are within your gate, so how will you escape?
The house of its planner Jezebel cannot stand; you have taken possession of the inheritance by blood, so how will you be saved?
The Lord searches out your iniquity, and exposes you, and holds you accountable for murder and plunder and all evils.
And in justice He will destroy your dwelling filled with iniquity, and will take vengeance on you in uprightness, because you have provoked Him [6].

St. Jacob of Serugh: Fiery Elijah and King Ahaziah (2 Kgs 1): Ahaziah the son of Ahab and Jezebel heard about his parents, whose blood the dogs licked, because they had turned aside from the way of truth. Now, since he did not benefit from the experience of his parents, just as discipline came upon his father so that the dogs licked his blood, the prophetic voice came to him: "Thou shalt not come down off that bed."
v The messengers of the son of Ahab heard from Elijah, and returned to him bearing bad news (2 Kgs 1:5).
They entered, and told him all they had heard from Elijah, and they repeated before him that he would not come down from his bed (2 Kgs 1:6).
They carried to this sick pagan the tidings of death, and wounded his heart with the word they had heard from Elijah...
He watched for opportunities to close the way of idolatry, lest the circumcised sons of Abraham walk in it.
He gathered them from every side to God, after they had been scattered among the idols of the Canaanites.
He brought them back from the strange ways, to walk in the great way of the King their Lord.
When they went out in the paths of the Amorites, the zealous one arose and brought them back to his God.
The flock of Isaac left the river of living water (Jer 2:13), to go and drink of the water of evil which destroys it.
Elijah, the good shepherd, drove it away (from there), lest it drink from the springs that spew forth death.

entries.section: 1. In praise of the prophet Elijah

paragraphs.text: The poison of the serpent was in the river of the Canaanites, and (Elijah) watched every day lest the flock drink from it [7].
St. Jacob of Serugh: And you heard a rebuke in Sinai, and in Horeb sentences of vengeance [7].

Ahab told his wife Jezebel what Elijah had done, and how he had killed the priests of Baal, and she was greatly enraged and resolved to kill him. Elijah was compelled to flee to Beersheba which belongs to Judah, where an angel sustained him there. The Spirit led him to go to Mount Horeb, the mountain on which Moses received the Law (1 Kgs 19).

entries.section: 1. In praise of the prophet Elijah

paragraphs.text: v After the preparation of forty days of fasting Elijah saw the Lord on Mount Horeb. And he heard from Him the words: "What doest thou here, Elijah?" Here the saying is very close to the saying: "Adam, where art thou?" in the Book of Genesis. The aim of the latter is to stir the fears of one who had eaten and was lost, while the former is addressed to a fasting servant with tenderness and love [8].
St. Jerome v The prophet walked in the wilderness forty days (1 Kgs 19:8), and reached Horeb, the mountain of the Lord, and settled there.
He walked and accomplished the way of perfection with diligence, and entered the place in which Moses was enlightened.

entries.section: 1. In praise of the prophet Elijah

paragraphs.text: He lodged in a cave (1 Kgs 19:9), whose name and work were beloved, and it is preferred to him who dwells in it above the palace of kings [9].
St. Jacob of Serugh: You anointed kings for retribution, and prophets to minister after you [8].

The kings whom Elijah anointed are Hazael and Jehu, and as for the prophets, he anointed Elisha his disciple. And since it is recorded of Obadiah that he hid a hundred prophets from the slaughter ordered by Queen Jezebel, perhaps all these prophets or some of them were anointed by the prophet Elijah (1 Kgs 18:3-4).
You were taken up in a whirlwind of fire, in a chariot of fiery horses [9].
v Let us then speak of the ascent of this beautiful one, and of the splendid chariot which came down to him on the earth.
And of the fleshly one who was found worthy to dwell with the spiritual, and of the earthy one who did not return to the earth to become dust.
And of the lowly one who directed his way toward the heavenly ones, and of the son of our race who left us and mingled with the angels.

entries.section: 1. In praise of the prophet Elijah

paragraphs.text: And of the wonder that seized the earth, because the heavenly ones snatched one from her bosom, to be with them among their choirs [10].

St. Jacob of Serugh: And you shall come to rebuke at the appointed time, as it is written, to pacify the wrath of God before its fury, and to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob [10].
The wisdom of the prophet Elijah declares that he acts in everything at the appropriate time.

entries.section: 1. In praise of the prophet Elijah

paragraphs.text: Blessed are those who saw you, and those who have fallen asleep in love, for we also shall surely live (after death) [11].

v The union of the body with the soul prepares it to appear to the light out of the darkness of the womb. But the union of the soul with the body (its submission to it) confines it in the darkness of the body. Therefore we must not spare the body, but subdue it as an enemy of the soul and an adversary to it. For absorption in delicious foods stirs up evil passions, while a fasting stomach quiets the passions and rescues the soul [11].
St. Anthony the Great

entries.section: 2. In praise of the prophet Elisha

paragraphs.text: 13 And Elijah was covered in the whirlwind; and Elisha was filled with his spirit, and in his days he was not moved for fear of any ruler, neither could any bring him under. 14 No word could overcome him, and after his death his body prophesied. 15 He did wonders in his life, and at his death his works were marvellous. 16 For all this the people repented not, neither departed they from their sins, till they were spoiled and carried out of their land, and were scattered through all the earth, 17 and there was left a small people, and a ruler in the house of David, 18 some of them did that which was pleasing, and some multiplied sins.

After the ascent of the prophet Elijah to heaven, the prophetic work was received by his disciple Elisha, who desired that two portions of his teacher's spirit might rest upon him so that he might fulfill his mission and face the growing tide of evil. God granted that there be accomplished at his hands double the miracles which his teacher had performed, to affirm the need of society for increased work because of the increase of corruption.
v O distinguished ones, listen to me, and I will speak further about the disciple who has amazed me by the beauty of his way.
His teacher (the prophet Elijah) overcame me, so I fell silent about him and did not describe him, and this one also stirs me by his wonder and his conduct.
Yes, in truth he is the disciple of that beautiful one, and his beauty springs from his deeds wherever he went.
He wrought a victory over the bad waters which he healed, and gave health to the sick and desolate land.
By his prophecy he put an end to death and restrained it, so it went out after seeing his might [12].
St. Jacob of Serugh: Elijah was covered by the whirlwind, and Elisha was filled with his spirit, and in his days he was not shaken or trembled before any ruler, and no one subdued [13] him [12].

The last scene in the life of the prophet Elijah reveals to us the depth of the tender feelings which Elisha held for his teacher. And as he realized that the end was near, he resolved to be with him to the end. Nothing could persuade him to leave Elijah, and when he asked him what he should do for him before he was taken from him, he asked for the portion of the firstborn son, a double portion of his teacher's spirit (2 Kgs 2:9). He saw his teacher in a terrifying sight, so he rent his clothes, and took up the mantle of his teacher, and returned to the Jordan, striking the water to see whether the spirit of Elijah had really rested upon him, and when the water was parted he crossed over on dry ground. By this the sons of the prophets who were watching the scene from the hills realized that the spirit of Elijah had rested on Elisha, so they bowed to him in respect and submission (2 Kgs 2:12-15). Here Elisha began his ministry which lasted about fifty years, for it extended throughout the reign of Jehoram and Jehu and Jehoahaz and Joash.
No word could overcome him, and even after the sleep of death his body prophesied [13].

entries.section: 2. In praise of the prophet Elisha

paragraphs.text: He did wonders in his life, and even after his death his works were astonishing [14].

When the ten tribes (the northern kingdom) were split off and rebelled against God, and set up temples and altars and worship according to their own desire, He sent to them fiery Elijah and his disciple Elisha the prophet, the wonder-worker. Believers do not need to have wonders performed; rather they are given to unbelievers. The Apostle says: "Wherefore tongues are for a sign, not to them that believe, but to them that believe not: but prophesying (preaching) serveth not for them that believe not, but for them which believe" (1 Cor 14:22).

Elisha was a wonder-worker even after his death, for his dry bones raised a dead man who was cast into the grave (2 Kgs 13:21). The Lord allowed this miracle so that, when the people fell under captivity and counted themselves like the dead, they might know that God sends them one who will bring them back to the Promised Land. For the man of God is sanctified in all that is his, even his bones after his death. St. Augustine says that the prophecies did not stop at being declared by words, but were also given by symbolic acts [14] such as the raising of the dead man by the bones of Elisha.
v The prophets spoke of him in amazement (and said): The spirit of his teacher came upon him and overflowed (2 Kgs 2:15).

They asked him to heal, as from a spiritual physician, the sick (corrupt) and desolate land which was barren. They saw power in him, so they asked him to heal the bad waters, and to relieve the whole land by his proven virtue. They said to him: The village is good and its location beautiful, but the waters are bad and the land is desolate and distresses us (2 Kgs 2:19).

entries.section: 2. In praise of the prophet Elisha

paragraphs.text: He said to them: Bring me a new cruse, and put salt therein; and they did as he said. He took it and went out to the spring, and cast the salt into the bad waters, and healed them because they were sick (2 Kgs 2:20-22) [15].

entries.section: 2. In praise of the prophet Elisha

paragraphs.text: St. Jacob of Serugh: The prophet Elisha died, and was buried in the grave, and his body decayed, and nothing remained but a heap of dry bones. But these bones bear witness to the spirit of power which the prophet lived and which death could not crush. After the death of the prophet Elisha, when the raiders of Moab cast a man into his grave, and the corpse touched the bones of Elisha, he lived and stood up on his feet (2 Kgs 13:21). St. Ephrem the Syrian says: [None of the prophets after his death raised a man. Therefore we see that the spirit of Elijah rested doubled upon Elisha. In fact, the authority which the Lord gave to the bones of Elisha is a symbol and seed of the resurrection. And the honor that was given to them shows the glory which the bodies of the saints will have, being clothed with it on the day of the resurrection of all the dead [16].]
v The dust of the righteous, which was scattered in Hades upon the dust, is chosen gold, and a spring full of good things.
The pure body, which the lusts did not defile, is the dust of the righteous, and it is a treasure of relics in which there is tenderness for him who approaches it...
Every day a sweet fragrance rises spiritually from their bones, which no ointment resembles.
In their corpses the divine indwelling dwells like the Kingdom in a temple of gold and pearls.
From their bodies flows Gihon (Gen 2:13) for all the healings, which used to grow beside the tree of life (Gen 2:19)..
From the sinner a foul smell rises at his death, but the righteous man is the chosen censer of God...

entries.section: 2. In praise of the prophet Elisha

paragraphs.text: He fell asleep in God, and behold, life awakens in him every day; he died to the world and became alive to his Lord, the joy of the face [17].
St. Jacob of Serugh: And with all this the people did not repent, nor did they cease from their sins, until their land was seized, and they were scattered in all the earth [15].

He speaks here of the Assyrian captivity of the kingdom of Israel, when the kingdom of Judah, small in number, remained, and the ruler of the house of David was Hezekiah king of Judah (2 Chr 30:1-12).
And there was left but a small remnant, and a ruler of the house of David.
Some of them did that which was good, and some multiplied sins [16].
By "some of them" he means those who did the virtues of King Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah.

entries.section: 2. In praise of the prophet Elisha

paragraphs.text: v Those who strive toward the virtuous life and the life of love for God are zealous toward (acquiring) the virtues of the Spirit as possessions whose ownership cannot be transferred to another, and which bring eternal rest. These use temporal things merely because they are necessary (and not out of luxury), and according to the will and providence of God, and they use them with joy and all gratitude, even if it be only enough for subsistence. For the lavish table feeds bodies, since they are material, but the knowledge of God, and victory over self, and goodness, and doing good to all, and compassion and meekness... these glorify the soul [18].
St. Anthony the Great

entries.section: 3. In praise of King Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah

paragraphs.text: 19 Hezekiah fortified his city, and brought in water into the midst thereof; he dug the rock with iron, and built wells for the water. 20 In his days Sennacherib came up, and sent Rabshakeh; and he came and lifted up his hand against Zion, and boasted in his pride. 21 Then trembled their hearts and hands, and they were in pain as women in travail. 22 But they called upon the merciful Lord, stretching out their hands toward Him; and the Holy One quickly heard them out of heaven, 23 and delivered them by the hand of Isaiah. 24 He smote the camp of the Assyrians, and His angel destroyed them. 25 For Hezekiah had done the thing that pleased the Lord, and was strong in the ways of David his father, which Isaiah the prophet commanded him, who was great and faithful in his vision. 26 In his days the sun went backward, and he lengthened the king's life. 27 He saw by an excellent spirit what should come to pass at the last, and he comforted them that mourned in Zion. 28 He showed what should come to pass for ever, and secret things or ever they came.
